sections.h2: List, sell privately or sell for cash
sections.html:
Each route can work, and each one ends at the same Suffolk County recording desk. About 87.6% of Lindenhurst homes are lived in by their owners, so most sellers here are parting with a family house they have held for years.

  • Broker listing: a good fit once the house shows well and you can ride out offers, inspections and mortgage approval.
  • Private sale: avoids a broker fee, though you screen buyers and run the contract steps with your attorney.
  • Cash sale: fits a house with repair needs, a rental permit gap, an estate to settle or a firm deadline, since the buyer accepts the property as it stands.

Condition moves the price under every option, so collect at least two opinions of value before you decide.

Lindenhurst is an incorporated village inside the Town of Babylon, on Long Island's South Shore with the Great South Bay along its southern edge. It covers about 3.75 square miles of land. A typical home is valued at $521,500, and households average 3.21 people.

Much of the housing dates from the postwar surge, when population jumped from 8,644 in 1950 to 28,359 in 1970. Water shapes the real estate too. In October 2012 Hurricane Sandy flooded more than half of the village's streets, with water up to about 6 feet south of Montauk Highway. Buyers who ask about flood history on the south side are asking a fair question, so gather your elevation, insurance and repair records before showings or an offer review.

A Lindenhurst address comes with village-run services a buyer will ask about. The village runs its own Building Department, Code Enforcement, Public Works for highway and sanitation, a Parks Department and a Village Court. A posted sanitation calendar covers pickup days, and the village has a marina, Irmisch Park along the water and its own stop on the Babylon Branch of the Long Island Rail Road.

Homes with a second unit fall under the village's Two-Family Review Board and a two-family page in the Building Department. If your house has an accessory apartment, ask the department how it is classified before you list.

sections.h2: Renting out the house before you sell
sections.html:
Lindenhurst requires a rental permit. A first-time application must be notarized and is followed by an inspection. Permits are renewed every two years unless the permit says otherwise, and renewal also triggers an inspection.

Inspections are booked with the Building Department, which lists set weekday windows on Tuesdays and Wednesdays for residential rentals and a separate schedule for mixed-use rentals. A landlord preparing to sell should check that the permit on file matches how the house is actually used. Before a contract is signed, ask the department what it holds on your address.

If the permit has lapsed, renew it and pass the inspection before you list, or tell buyers plainly that it is outstanding. Either way, you will want the answer settled before an offer arrives.

Lindenhurst owners get several tax bills, because the village taxes separately from the Town of Babylon and the school district. The village bill is a once-a-year tax, mailed by March 1 and due April 1. The village Tax Department accepts it only in full. A payment after April 1 draws a 5 percent penalty plus a $2.00 fee, and the charge keeps growing monthly.

The village Assessment Department prepares the roll for almost 10,000 parcels and handles exemptions for senior citizens, former service members, firefighters and volunteer ambulance workers, non-profit organizations and clergy. Those exemptions reduce only the village tax bill. Senior applications require income of no more than $37,400, are renewed every year and are due by October 1.

  • Village grievance: the window opens each November 1 and closes on Grievance Day, the third Tuesday of November, which is November 17 this year.
  • Town of Babylon grievance: filed with the Town Assessor, due by the third Tuesday in May, with forms available from mid-April.
  • Small claims: if the Town's Board of Assessment Review denies a grievance, a small claims petition goes to the Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead.

Tell the village Assessment Department when ownership changes or a mortgage is satisfied, so the next bill goes to the right party. Tax information is not given out by phone, so request a tax search by email using the village's request form.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Suffolk County
sections.html:
The Suffolk County Clerk figures transfer tax at $2.00 per $500 of the price, counting any fraction of $500. Recording fees run $245 plus $5.00 per page. Check the clerk's current deed fee schedule before you budget, since the amounts can change.

When a residential price reaches $1,000,000, a 1% mansion tax is also due from the buyer, paid in cash or by certified check made out to the Suffolk County Clerk. The tax map number you need for the forms comes from the Town Assessor, which for Lindenhurst is the Town of Babylon's office in Town Hall on East Sunrise Highway.

The base transfer tax falls on the seller, though the contract can shift it. After closing, end your STAR registration, since owners are asked to do that on a sale. Your attorney or title company normally prepares the deed package, so your job is to sign and to have your tax statements and mortgage payoff ready.

Allow time for the notary and the filing. The deed has to be signed and acknowledged before it goes to the clerk, and the transfer tax return and payment follow soon after delivery, so ask your attorney which deadline they are working to.

sections.h2: Preparing a Lindenhurst house for a quick sale
sections.html:
A short list keeps a fast sale on track. Pull the rental permit and any two-family paperwork if they apply, and ask the Building Department what is on file. Collect flood, insurance and repair records for the south side of the village. Request a tax search from the village by email and note which exemptions you receive, since the buyer will lose them.

With a cash offer there is no mortgage approval or appraisal to wait on, so these papers set the pace. Compare the cash price with your best listing estimate after commission and months of carrying costs, and have a New York attorney read the contract before you sign.

faqs.q: What is the due date for the Lindenhurst village tax?
faqs.a: Village tax is due April 1, and bills go out by March 1. It is a once-a-year tax, payment is accepted only in full, and a late payment adds 5 percent and a $2.00 fee.

faqs.q: What are the Lindenhurst grievance dates?
faqs.a: The village's Grievance Day is the third Tuesday of November, which is November 17 in 2026. The Town of Babylon runs its own process, ending on the third Tuesday of May.

faqs.q: Is a rental permit needed for a Lindenhurst rental?
faqs.a: Yes. Lindenhurst requires a rental permit with a notarized first application and an inspection, and permits are renewed every two years. Ask the village Building Department about mixed-use properties, which have their own inspection hours.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for transfer tax on a Lindenhurst sale?
faqs.a: The seller carries the state's $2.00-per-$500 tax by default, though the contract can move it. A buyer pays the separate 1% mansion tax once a residential price hits $1,000,000.

faqs.q: Which exemptions does the village Assessment Department handle?
faqs.a: Exemptions for senior citizens, former service members, firefighters and volunteer ambulance workers, non-profit organizations and clergy. They reduce only the village tax bill. Senior applications need income of no more than $37,400 and are due by October 1 each year.
